::: {.lead-serif}
How speech and language technologies can be developed responsibly while respecting linguistic diversity, fairness, privacy, transparency, and social equity. I work at the intersection of speech technology, AI governance, and research ethics, combining technical expertise with perspectives from law, philosophy, and public policy.
:::

## Leadership and governance roles

- **2027**: Ethics Chair, [IEEE ASLI 2027](https://2027.ieeeasli.org/organizing-committee/) (IEEE International Conference on Audio, Speech, and Language Intelligence), Singapore
- **2025–2026**: [Ethics Chair, INTERSPEECH](posts/2026-10-01-interspeech-2026-ethics-2026/index.qmd), overseeing ethical standards for the field's largest conference
- **2025–2026**: Member, Ethics Committee, International Speech Communication Association (ISCA)
- **2025–2026**: Management Committee Member (Netherlands), Grassroots of Digital Europe (GRADE), COST Action CA21141
- **2023–present**: Working Group Member, Coalition for Advancing Research Assessment (CoARA), *Ethics and Research Integrity Policy in Responsible Research Assessment for Data and Artificial Intelligence* (ERIP)
- **2025–present** and **2018–2020**: Chair, Ethics Committee, Campus Fryslân, University of Groningen

## Current projects

- Co-editing *Speech Tech Ethics*, a forthcoming book with Maggie Glass exploring ethical frameworks for speech and language technologies.
- Contributing to the CoARA working group on ethics and research integrity in research assessment for data and AI.
- Developing ethical guidelines and educational resources for speech technology research and teaching.
- Integrating AI ethics into speech technology curricula and professional training.

## Education and outreach

- *Research Ethics*, workshop for PhD students, Campus Fryslân Graduate School (November 2026)
- Organizer, Speech Tech Summer Schools (2023, 2024)
- Developed the module *GPT in the Classroom: Ethical Considerations* for my Senior Teaching Qualification (STQ), University of Groningen (2024)
- Professional training in AI ethics: *AI Empathy & Ethics*, University of California (2024); *AI: Ethics & Societal Challenges*, Lund University (2023)

- **2026**: [*Who Governs the Spoken Word? Speech Tech, Minoritized Languages, and the Limits of AI Law*](posts/2026-06-09-marginalized-knowledge-systems-warsaw/index.qmd). AI & Marginalized Knowledge Systems workshop, University of Warsaw
